# Appeal of Denial — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**Governing Policy:** Aetna CPB 0660 - Knee Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html)

**Member:** Rowan Carter
**Member ID:** W914903090
**Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Missouri
**Denial date:** 2026-08-19
**Reference number:** POC-5BA41AD17E-24277

Dear Aetna Appeals Review Team,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), reference number POC-5BA41AD17E-24277. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the medical record shows that my case meets Aetna's own published criteria for this surgery.

## The plan's criteria and how my records meet them

**1. This is a single-compartment case, which is what unicompartmental (partial) knee arthroplasty is for.**

Aetna's policy states:

> "unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is indicated when only 1 compartment is affected, and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is indicated when 2 or 3 compartments are affected."

My MRI from 2026-06-09 shows full-thickness cartilage loss with bone-on-bone apposition in the medial compartment only, with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes limited to that compartment. No other compartment is reported as affected. This is exactly the single-compartment presentation the policy describes as appropriate for a partial (unicompartmental) replacement, not a total knee replacement.

**2. I have completed the conservative therapy the policy requires.**

Aetna's policy states:

> "Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication) - with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year, including all of the following, unless contraindicated:"

My record shows 14 weeks of supervised, in-person physical therapy (16 visits, 2026-04-10 through 2026-07-17), documented in my physical therapy discharge note, along with 8 months of NSAID use with inadequate relief and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-17 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief. This is more than the 12 weeks the policy requires, and more than half of it was formal, in-person physical therapy.

**3. My symptoms and exam findings support that conservative care has not resolved the problem.**

Aetna's policy also states:

> "If conservative therapy is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such approach is not reasonable;"

While conservative therapy was appropriate and was tried, my record shows it did not adequately relieve my symptoms: 9 months of progressive pain unrelieved by rest, inability to climb stairs without assistance, waking 3-4 times nightly with pain, positive provocative testing, and pain-limited range of motion on exam. These findings, together with the bone-on-bone MRI findings in the weight-bearing medial compartment, document why continued non-surgical management is not expected to resolve the problem.

**4. Regarding the corticosteroid injection timing:**

I understand the policy also notes:

> "or Corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty;"

My injection was given on 2026-06-17. I am including this date so Aetna can confirm it falls outside the 12-week window before my planned surgery date of [PLANNED SURGERY DATE], as required by this provision.

I do not have any of the absolute contraindications described in the policy: my record shows no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

## Request

Based on the plan's own criteria, quoted above, and the clinical documentation in my file, I am asking Aetna to reconsider and approve this request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446). If any additional records are needed from Dr. Marchetti's office to complete this review, please let me know what is needed and I will ask that it be submitted promptly.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-15. I am submitting it through Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form as instructed, and I have confirmed the correct submission address on my denial letter. For reference, the general appeal channels I am aware of are:

- Online: aetna.com (Member Complaint and Appeal Form)
- Fax: 859-425-3379
- Phone: 1-800-872-3862, or the number on my member card

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

[Rowan Carter]
Member ID: W914903090
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
